long_biography.plain_text:
Croatian hotelier Goran Štrok changed his acquisition rules after losing money on two Scottish properties. Their small size made them difficult to operate profitably, so he decided to consider hotels with at least 28 bedrooms. He also wanted his Croatian investments to demonstrate professional standards in the country's rebuilding tourism industry.

At the Dubrovnik Palace, his wife Renata worked on the interiors while he oversaw the wider redevelopment. Staff trained before opening, and an experienced food and beverage manager was recruited to introduce a broader international menu. His approach extended beyond the building: a service agency arranged airport transfers, excursions and conference business for the hotel group.
